thread:
Samir: Quick heads-up — Proofpoint execs want a concrete reserved GPU + autoscale plan for the enterprise commit. They also attached a security questionnaire that's holding signatures. cc @Marta @Liam
Marta: Do we have a throughput profile from them? p95/p99 SLOs?
Samir: From the architect call: baseline ~600 rps, expected marketing spikes up to 2.5k rps for ~15m windows, avg request ~150 tokens in + 50 tokens out. p95 latency target 300ms, p99 800ms. They prefer single-region but want AZ fallback.
Liam: Quick calc — assume our serving stack gives ~60k output tokens/s per A100-equivalent GPU for their model (mixed quant). With 150 tokens/request => ~400 req/s per GPU sustained. For peaks 2.5k rps -> ~7 GPUs sustained. Add 20% safety -> 9 GPUs. Recommend reserved commit = 8 GPUs + burst pool up to 16 (autoscale).
Marta: Can we express that as a deploy policy we can hand to sales? They want simple buckets: committed, burst, prewarm.
Liam: Yes. Example policy (high level):
```
committed: 8 gpus
burst_limit: 16 gpus
min_active: 4 instances (HA across AZs)
prewarm_window: 300s
burst_policy: credit_based with sustained cooldown 900s
```
Nora: Security Qs — they asked about network topology, KMS, and audit logs. Dedicated reserved will be easiest (VPC peering + KMS). Private deploy is possible but 2–3 week lead. Dedicated can be ready in ~3 business days once networking completed. That's a blocker until we have their CIDRs and IAM contacts.
Samir: Perfect. Sales ask: what pricing to pitch for the commit? Also what happens if spike > burst_limit?
Marta: Propose commit discount at ~30% off on-demand for the 8-GPU monthly commitment, overage billed at on-demand per-GPU rate, and burst credits consumed after committed. If spike > burst_limit, requests degrade to best-effort: model fallback (smaller model) or queue with 503-based backpressure. Need to confirm auto-fallback policy.
Liam: Auto-fallback plan: primary model -> lighter quantized variant -> fallback to hosted lower-cost model (if enabled). We can configure routing rules to prefer latency SLOs and then cost.
Samir: Can you put the autoscale conf snippet I can paste into the SOW?
Liam: Sure — paste below (keep as example):
```
autoscale:
  min_instances: 4
  committed_instances: 8
  max_instances: 16
  target_rps_per_instance: 400
  prewarm_seconds: 300
  burst_policy: credit_based
  az_distribution: spread
  fallback_on_capacity_exhaust: enable_model_fallback
```
Marta: Sales note — include clause: we require network info 72h before go-live for prewarm and final capacity test. Also ask legal to add a rollback SLA for model fallback windows.
Nora: Security note — for the questionnaire items: SOC2 date, KMS provider (AWS KMS), HSM option, key rotation policy, and audit logs retention (90 days default, longer available). I'll attach the redacted answers by EOD.
Samir: Great. Action items: (1) Liam to finalize sizing calc and put into SOW (2) Marta to draft pricing bands + 72h network requirement (3) Nora to upload security responses and test plan.
Marta: I'll draft SOW snippet and post here for quick approval. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: reserved-pool "proofpoint-commit-1930056789" created (8 GPUs committed, burst cap 16) — pending network handshake.
Samir: Awesome, thanks. I'll loop in their infra lead for CIDR and peering details.
Liam: One more — recommend a prewarm run: 30m sustained at 80% peak to warm KV caches ~ 24h before critical campaign. Add to SOW as optional line item.
Marta: Noted, will add.
Samir: Closing — will update thread after we get CIDRs and signed SOW.
